newsitem.title: UK: BT firms as market celebrates Telefonica deal.
newsitem.headline: BT firms as market celebrates Telefonica deal.

text.p: Shares in British Telecommunications Plc advanced 4p to 446-1/2p on Friday, after news that it is to form a global alliance with its merger partner MCI Communications Corp and Telefonica de Espana SA.

"This opens up Latin America for BT and it's good news to see Telefonica defecting to Concert from Unisource," said one analyst. The combined BT/MCI group will be called Concert. Telefonica is withdrawing from Unisource, the group name for AT&T Corp and three European telecoms companies.

Jim McCafferty, analyst at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said, "This is good news although it has been expected in the market and it looks like Telefonica has paid 440p for BT share, which should lend some support."

Speculation that the companies would form a global alliance was rife after news on Monday of a tie-up between Concert and Portugal Telecom and on Tuesday of a tie-up between Telefonica and Portugal Telecom.

"This was well leaked. Everyone's been expecting this since the Portugal deals early this week but share prices can always increase when the news is actually in black and white," said another telecoms analyst.
By the London opening, BT shares had put on another penny to stand 5p higher in a weaker overall market. BT was the most heavily traded stock in the market.
